checks: Concavity and positive denominator give 0<a≤1. Arithmetic–geometric mean bounds −log a by the logarithmic Jensen gap. Fixed endpoint log integrals and the globally convex extension of −log L compare the two gaps in the required direction. Jensen for 1−exp(−dx) gives the nonlinear mass bound.

The tangent extensions of −log t and −t^p remain convex and decreasing on the full real line. Taking the maximum of the affine-composed extensions gives their correct values on C. This justifies the use of full physical convex order without assuming global positivity of the affine pieces.

For 0<p≤1, L^p and the scalar pth power are concave. The probability L(b)^p dπ/T_p gives expectation of a^p at least c_p/T_p. Convexity of exponent d/p then gives the first weighted estimate. The derivative of T−c^r T^(1−r) is 1+(r−1)c^r T^(−r), and the tangent at one gives the linear endpoint bound.

For positive affine q the maximizing variational parameter is 1+log(q/L), uniformly bounded on C. The bounded supremum over affine functions gives a globally finite convex extension. Uniform convergence for q+ε justifies the comparison for q≥0 on C.

Expanding the relative entropy identity uses q_i/L_i=(q(b)/V)(p_i/s_i), so the constant term is log[L(b)/V]=−log a. Entropy is zero exactly at equality of the two probability vectors and hence exactly at equality of the endpoint ratios. At q(b)=0 affineness and nonnegativity force both endpoint weights and the local gap to vanish.

For T_q>0 use the probability q(b)dπ/T_q and the same exponential Jensen inequality. The affine total is fixed by the marginals, so the old gap supplies the bound. Zero total mass or zero affine weight gives zero errors without division.

overlap.comparison: The logarithmic nonlinear payment is already proved for a proper repaired branch embedded in an actual normal-preserving surface martingale, with an endpoint capacity/residual and source identity. This theorem gives it for arbitrary compact physical fixed-marginal tuple laws and adds power and affine weights.

For strictly positive affine q, apply its row algebra to the equal two-point row at b to get the same KL decomposition and comparison of the affine gap. This theorem adds the nonlinear discount payment, zero q support and direct comparison between arbitrary given midpoint laws.
Treats the different one-sided perspective and the weight (q−L)_+ for convex q. Its error weight, entropy functional and endpoint denominator differ from the full affine q log(q/L) result.

readability: The proof compares separable logarithmic Jensen gaps under fixed endpoint laws. The tuple discount itself is used only pointwise and inside the resulting Jensen estimate.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The fixed-marginal convex-order argument proves all three nonlinear discount payments on the same coupling, including zero affine weights.
